sponsors-first.text: The United States and Japan argued that extending reporting ensures accurate information on Houthi attacks, while Algeria valued the reports but abstained due to concerns over resolution implementation and self-defence misuse.

algeria-first.text: Algeria's abstention was due to implementation concerns and misuse of self-defence, whereas the US and Japan supported extending reporting to secure accurate information on Houthi attacks threatening commerce and humanitarian aid.

action-first.text: Algeria's rationale for abstention focused on implementation concerns and misuse of self-defence, whereas the adopted action merely extended reporting without new military authorization.

action-second.text: Algeria's abstention rationale regarding implementation concerns and self-defence misuse contrasts with the adopted action's neutral extension of reporting without new military authorization.
